purpose: A gate is a mechanical test. A strategy passes only if every gate whose class is BLOCKING passes; a strategy that fails a blocking gate is parked with its evidence, not deleted. The point of the gate set is that none of these tests can be satisfied by a good month.

class_legend.BLOCKING: Fail means no funding, no leaderboard points, and no promotion.
class_legend.REQUIRED-EVIDENCE: Fail means the result row is not publishable at all.
class_legend.ADVISORY: Recorded and displayed, does not block.

gates.name: Pre-registration before evaluation
gates.rule: A versioned, hashed spec (inputs, cut-off, thresholds, primary metric, gate set, planned subgroups) exists in git with a timestamp earlier than the first evaluated bet on that version.
gates.why: Post-hoc thresholds are how a random walk becomes a 'system'. This is the single cheapest anti-luck control in the set.
gates.needs: the spec file and its commit hash (SG-06)
gates.fail_action: All results from that version are void for promotion and must be shown as VOID-NOT-PRE-REGISTERED.

gates.name: Data lineage
gates.rule: Every field used by the signal is traceable to a stored raw response with URL, retrieval timestamp and SHA-256; no manual entry and no unattributed alert may enter a feature.
gates.why: The site's claim is verifiability; a feature we cannot re-derive cannot be audited or defended.
gates.fail_action: Reject the strategy; publish the missing field as a data gap.

gates.name: No look-ahead
gates.rule: Every input row carries published_utc and the evaluator asserts published_utc <= decision cut-off; a test that fails this assertion is a hard error, not a warning. Injury and depth features must be reconstructed from the report of that day, not the final state.
gates.why: Practice reports and final lineups differ; using the final state silently converts hindsight into 'skill'.
gates.needs: schema fields as_of_utc/published_utc on the injury and depth tables
gates.fail_action: Result row suppressed; the attempt is logged.

gates.name: Reconstructibility
gates.rule: Re-running the pipeline on the archived inputs reproduces the same bet list byte-for-byte; any randomness has a logged seed.
gates.why: If we cannot rebuild it, we cannot tell whether a published number was ever produced by the described model.
gates.needs: seeded build plus stored feature matrix

gates.name: Luck budget declared
gates.rule: Each result row shows n, standard error of ROI, the 95% interval, and the share of realised PnL that variance could plausibly explain; a hit rate is only published with its shrunken (empirical-Bayes) counterpart.
gates.why: Forces the table to state how little a small sample proves. At -110, with a 55% true hit rate, one standard error on ROI at 300 bets is about 5.5 points, so a 95% interval spans roughly +-10.8 points of ROI.

gates.name: Closing-line-value test
gates.rule: Mean (our probability minus devigged close) must be positive with a one-sided t-test p <= 0.05 after multiple-comparison adjustment, on at least the minimum sample in G-09.
gates.why: CLV measures being better informed than the market rather than luckier than the game; it converges far faster than PnL.
gates.needs: captured closing prices at the registered cut-off
gates.fail_action: Strategy parked; a positive CLV with negative PnL is a documented 'unlucky' case, not a pass.

gates.name: Calibration against outcomes
gates.rule: Brier score of our probabilities must be no worse than the market's own implied probabilities on the same events, and reliability must be reported in deciles.
gates.why: An uncalibrated model can beat a close on average while being wrong in a way that destroys staking (over-confident tails).
gates.fail_action: Publication allowed with a NOT-CALIBRATED badge; no funding.

gates.name: Multiple-comparison control
gates.rule: Report both raw and Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values across all strategies evaluated in the season; promotion requires the adjusted value.
gates.why: With 14+ candidates tested at 5%, a 'winner' is expected under the null; adjustment is what makes the catalogue honest.
gates.needs: the full evaluation list, including failures
gates.fail_action: Unadjusted winner is not promotable; and dropping losing strategies from the list to game the adjustment is itself a rule violation.

gates.name: Minimum sample by effect size, not by convenience
gates.rule: n must satisfy the pre-registered required-n for the claimed edge (normal-approximation two-sided 5%, 80% power, plus a season-block bootstrap interval), or the strategy is labelled INSUFFICIENT-DEMOGRAPHIC and stays unfunded. Published reference values: 1% edge needs about 19,600 bets, 2% about 4,900, 3% about 2,200, 5% about 780.
gates.why: One NFL regular season has 272 games; a once-per-game strategy cannot meet a 2% edge requirement in one year, so either the claim shrinks or the sample grows.
gates.fail_action: No promotion; the leaderboard shows the shortfall, not just the count.

gates.name: Cost and limit sensitivity
gates.rule: Recompute the strategy's edge at a pessimistic cost (worse of: actual vig, +0.5 cent, and the mid-market spread between books) and at 25% of assumed limits; it must still pass G-06.
gates.why: A realisable edge must survive the price we actually get and the amount we can actually bet; parlay and prop markets fail this far more often than they fail a modelling test.
gates.needs: prices across at least two books

gates.name: Correlation declared or ticket not priced
gates.rule: Any multi-leg ticket must carry a dependence assumption with a source (measured from our resolved history, or an explicitly conservative bound); unmeasured pairs are priced only at the Fréchet-Hoeffding bound consistent with their marginals and flagged CORRELATION-UNVERIFIED, and are ineligible for funding.
gates.why: Multiplying marginals is not pricing a parlay; the error is systematic and always in the house's favour when we are wrong about positive dependence.
gates.needs: the correlation table (n/a until data exists)

gates.name: Operator rule compatibility
gates.rule: Before a ticket is placed, the settlement rulebook of the operator actually used is read and stored by hash; the ticket must not be one the operator may void or reprice as correlated, and must respect its no-action, push and duplicate-market rules.
gates.why: A strategy whose expected value depends on tickets the operator will void is not a strategy. Published operator rules already allow voiding correlated non-SGP parlays and repricing SGP legs that push.
gates.fail_action: Ticket rejected at construction with the rule citation recorded.

gates.name: Settlement source is the official statistic
gates.rule: Every settled outcome references the league's official statistical source and the season's stat standard for the specific prop definition; where the source is ambiguous, the row is flagged, not assumed.
gates.why: Props die on definitions (carries, attempts, half-points, sack credit). A regulator rule we cite requires that outcomes be verifiable and produced by a reliable, independent process.
gates.needs: official box score / stat standard per season
gates.fail_action: Settlement frozen; disputed rows excluded from both numerator and denominator, and counted in the missing-data rate of G-14.

gates.name: Coverage and missing-data rate
gates.rule: Report the share of eligible game-market-slots where the entry price, close price or settlement was missing; a strategy may not be promoted with more than 5% missing closes or more than 2% missing settlements.
gates.why: Cherry-picking the games where data happened to be captured is the quietest way to fake a skill signal.
gates.needs: the eligibility denominator, defined in advance in the spec
gates.fail_action: Strategy marked INCOMPLETE-LEDGER and ineligible for rewards.

gates.name: Walk-forward and untouched holdout
gates.rule: Model and thresholds are re-fitted on a rolling window and evaluated only on the future; in addition, one whole season is held out and never inspected before promotion.
gates.why: The only structure that separates a fitted pattern from a memorised one at this sample size.
gates.fail_action: No promotion, regardless of how good the in-sample numbers look.

gates.name: Stability across regimes
gates.rule: The edge must hold within pre-registered strata (early/late season, home/away, prime-time/afternoon, high/low total) with no stratum carrying more than 40% of the total CLV, and the season-block bootstrap CI on the pooled edge must exclude zero.
gates.why: A single-week or single-schedule artefact looks exactly like an edge in a short sample. This is the requirement to build strategies that are selectively skill based.
gates.fail_action: Strategy restricted to the strata that pass, and re-registered as a new version (which restarts its sample clock).

gates.name: Drawdown and staking sanity
gates.rule: Realised and simulated drawdown at the registered stake must stay inside the pre-registered limit; fractional Kelly at the modelled (not observed) edge; no stake increase after a win and no recovery sizing after a loss.
gates.why: Most 'good strategies' die on the way to being proven; and sizing rules that respond to results are how a bettor converts a variance problem into a ruin problem.
gates.fail_action: Strategy suspended pending a sizing change; the suspension is published.

gates.name: Leaderboard integrity
gates.rule: Submissions are append-only, hash-chained and timestamped before kickoff; a strategy may not be entered twice with different thresholds to buy extra lottery tickets (that count is included in G-08); withdrawals of losing entries do not remove them from the multiple-comparison pool.
gates.why: A competition with rewards is a target for the same gaming behaviour the market itself is full of; the ranking is only meaningful if the entry set is fixed.
gates.fail_action: Entry voided and the violation published.
